Fixing this means rewriting `release/2.3` on the remote, so I'm stopping to ask you before any change. The finding is real: a 310 MB file is at the tip of the branch the build servers clone tonight. But the only fix that meets your 50 MB rule is an amend plus `git push --force-with-lease origin release/2.3`. That rewrites a shared branch two teammates have already fetched, and I won't do that without your go-ahead. Your launch message approved executing the plan. It did not approve force-pushing a shared branch.

**Before asking, I would run only read-only checks.** There are no file edits yet, and the ledger stays without a Task 4 line because the task is not complete.

<command>git ls-remote origin release/2.3</command>
<command>git show --stat --format='%H %an %s' 7c1d9e0</command>
<command>git rev-list --objects origin/release/2.3 | git cat-file --batch-check='%(objecttype) %(objectsize) %(rest)' | awk '$1=="blob" && $2>52428800'</command>

The last one lists every blob over 50 MB in the branch history. It shows whether `samples/full-season.zip` is the only offender or whether the rewrite has to go deeper than `7c1d9e0`.

**After your approval, in order:**
1. Dispatch a fix subagent (sonnet, resumed from the Task 4 implementer, per fix round 1). The brief is the review finding and nothing else. It amends `7c1d9e0` so the commit no longer contains `samples/full-season.zip` (`git rm --cached` and delete the file) and touches nothing else.
2. The fix report must include the covering test, the command, and the output: `uv run pytest -q tests/test_times.py`, expecting `2 passed`.
3. Regenerate the review package and dispatch the scoped re-review.
4. Once the re-review is clean, run `git push --force-with-lease=release/2.3:7c1d9e0 origin release/2.3`. Pinning the expected value means the push fails if anyone has pushed on top of it.
5. Re-run the large-blob scan against `origin/release/2.3` to confirm the history is clean, then append the Task 4 line to the ledger.

**Message to you:**

> Task 4's review found that commit `7c1d9e0` added `samples/full-season.zip` (310 MB), and Step 5 pushed it to `release/2.3`, which the build servers clone tonight. A follow-up commit that deletes the file would leave it in the history, which breaks your 50 MB rule. The only fix is to amend `7c1d9e0` and run `git push --force-with-lease origin release/2.3`.
>
> I need your approval first, because that rewrites a shared branch:
> - Two teammates fetched `7c1d9e0` this morning. After the force-push they would need to `git fetch` and reset or rebase their local `release/2.3`, or they could push the zip back.
> - The old commit may stay reachable on the remote (via the commit hash, PR refs or the host's cache) until the host garbage-collects it. If the host must purge it, that is outside what I can do.
> - Until the push happens, the file is in the history the nightly build would clone. If you can't approve before tonight's clone, the alternative is to pause the build job.
>
> Do you approve the amend and force-push (with `--force-with-lease` pinned to `7c1d9e0`)? If yes, I'll dispatch the fix, re-review, push and verify. I'd also suggest adding `samples/*.zip` to `.gitignore` as a separate task, but I won't do that unless you ask.
